creditNotes.heading: Credit Notes
creditNotes.subtitle: Documents that credit part or all of an invoice that was already paid. Not the same as invoice credit.
creditNotes.explain: A credit note reverses part of an invoice that was already paid and is a numbered document the client receives. It is not invoice credit, which is balance a client spends on an invoice. The numbering (CN-0001) is a cautious default and has not been checked against any local law: check what your jurisdiction requires before relying on it.
creditNotes.blockedTopUp: A credit top-up is credit already. Refund a paid top-up by hand from the Refund tab.
creditNotes.blockedNotPaid: A credit note can only be issued on an invoice that was paid.
creditNotes.blockedNothingLeft: Earlier credit notes and refunds already cover the whole invoice.
creditNotes.linesInvalid: Every line needs a description, a price above zero and at least one unit.
creditNotes.methodHint: Account credit puts the value on the client's credit balance. A gateway refund pays it back through the gateway that took the money, as one refund of the invoice.
creditNotes.reasonHint: Printed on the credit note, so the client reads it.
creditNotes.reasonPlaceholder: Why the credit note is issued
creditNotes.reasonRequired: Give a reason for the credit note.
creditNotes.overCredit: This is more than the invoice can still be credited.
creditNotes.emptyForInvoice: No credit notes were issued against this invoice.
creditNotes.voidMessage: Void credit note {number}? It keeps its number and stays on record. Account credit it gave comes off the client's balance, and the invoice can be credited again.
creditNotes.voidRefundBlocked: This note was paid out as a gateway refund. The refund cannot be taken back, so it cannot be voided.
creditNotes.voidReasonPlaceholder: Why the credit note is voided
creditNotes.voidReasonRequired: Give a reason for voiding the credit note.
